title: KPI ingest demux and adaptive labeler for inference telemetry
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Scope: Build an ingest-side demultiplexer and adaptive labeler that accepts mixed Prometheus and OpenTelemetry (OTel) envelopes from inference serving nodes and normalizes them into a compact per-request KPI stream for downstream SLI/SLO calculation and dashboards.

Goals:
- Accept OTLP/Prom remote_write inputs at the edge proxy and demux them into: latency buckets, token counts, error flags, model variant, route id, tenant id, and sampling tags.
- Apply adaptive cardinality reduction (label coalescing + dynamic sampling) to keep per-tenant cardinality within quotas while preserving tail latency signal.
- Emit two outputs: (1) enriched OTLP metrics for long-term storage and model-level histogram rollups, (2) a compact per-request KPI envelope (protobuf-lite JSON) routed to the KPI aggregator.
- Provide trace hooks that attach request trace IDs and span anchors when available, enabling correlation with spans for cold-start attribution.

Non-goals:
- Do not replace existing Prometheus remote_write pipeline; this is an additional adapter that can sit in front of it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest adapter handles 20k RPS of metric envelopes in staging with <200ms p95 processing latency and <2% additional error rate.
- Cardinality reduction limits new label combinations per tenant to the configured quota (default 1k/day) and exposes per-tenant telemetry.
- End-to-end test: synthetic traffic produces correct per-request KPI envelopes consumed by KPI aggregator, and dashboards show matching latency/error numbers within 2% of ground truth.
- Backwards-compatible with existing dashboard queries (translation layer implemented).

Design notes:
- Parser: use fastpath OTLP binary parsing for envelopes; fallback to Prometheus remote_write parsing.
- Demux rules: routing by envelope type, then by top-level label prefix (e.g., route:, model:, variant:).
- Labeler: rule engine (YAML-driven) that contains matchers + coalescing policies; runtime-configurable via console.
- Sampling: hybrid deterministic reservoir sampling for high-cardinality labels, with burst smoothing for short-lived spikes.
- Trace hooks: when span_id/trace_id present, attach as exemplar and include a compact trace anchor in KPI envelope.
- Backpressure: expose a per-tenant token-bucket and rejection path that returns structured hint headers for retries.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Canary deploy in staging, capture metrics and verify dashboards. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kpi-ingest/pull/312
2) Limited canary in production for low-traffic tenants (flagged) for 72 hours.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% of tenant traffic, monitor SLOs and cardinality metrics.
4) Full rollout when signal stable for 7 days.

Observability & testing:
- Add internal telemetry: processing latencies, coalesced-label counts, per-tenant rejection rate, exemplar attach rate.
- Provide a debug endpoint that replays original envelope and transformed KPI envelope.
- Unit and integration tests included; load test harness in kpi-loadbench repo.
